In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C. elegan’s rIIS extends lifespan comparably through two genetically separable pathways: one that is dauer-related and another that is not.
rIIS extends lifespan in C. elegans by activating dauer-related and -independent mechanisms, and that both of these mechanisms can be relevant to understanding healthy aging.
the IIS system is the major regulator of lifespan in C. elegans but not in humans, and that the IIS pathway in humans is not involved in the control of lifespan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insulin/IGFI-signaling pathway is a major determinant of longevity and healthspan in C. elegans.
rIIS is a powerful tool to study longevity, dauer, and healthspan in C. elegans.
we have made a significant contribution to our knowledge of the mechanisms of aging in C. elegans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C. elegan rIIS is a powerful paradigm to understand healthy aging in humans, but that the dauer program is not required for this process.
the dauer program in C. elegans can be uncoupled genetically from the rIIS lifespan extension program, and that dauer-related pathways can be important in extending healthspan.
the C. elegans dauer state, and the mechanisms that underlie it, have a major influence on the aging of the worm.
